page.geo: A website is not only design. Slovak buyers have their own habits, payment methods and expectations, and Slovak law has its own requirements on company details, cookies and data protection. A studio building your site from another country cannot know that. In Bratislava we can meet in person, the invoice carries a Slovak company number, and when something has to be sorted with an authority or a supplier, I speak their language.

faq.q: How much does a website cost?
faq.a: A simple landing page with contacts from 1 500€, a full website with booking or time slots, email on your domain and enquiry tracking from 3 500€, an e-shop from 5 000€. Hourly rate 35€. I state the exact price after the first conversation and do not change it later.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Ten working days on average, with 90% of projects delivered within 15. A larger shop or portal takes longer and I say so upfront.

faq.q: Do I need to prepare a detailed brief?
faq.a: No. That is exactly what holds most companies up, so I propose the solution based on a short conversation about your goals.

faq.q: WordPress or custom-built?
faq.a: Whichever fits. WordPress where you will manage content yourself and ready-made solutions suffice. Custom (PHP, Python, JS) where speed, unusual functionality or integrations are needed.

faq.q: What is included beyond the site itself?
faq.a: Domain and hosting setup, mail on your own domain, spam-protected forms, GA4 and Tag Manager tracking, a Consent Mode v2 cookie banner, basic SEO setup and six months of technical support.

faq.q: Do you work outside Bratislava?
faq.a: Yes, across Slovakia and neighbouring countries. In Bratislava we can meet in person; with remote clients I work online, and it makes no difference to the result.

faq.q: Do you build online stores?
faq.a: Yes. A store from €5,000 with cart, payment gateway, shipping and a Merchant Center feed for Google Shopping. For wholesale: per-customer price lists and orders without public prices.

faq.q: Custom build or a template?
faq.a: A template is enough when the site is a business card and you will manage the content yourself. Custom pays off when the site has to do work: bookings, slots, a client area, a link to stock or a calendar. The difference is not the design but what the site can do and how fast it loads.

faq.q: Can you rebuild an existing site?
faq.a: Yes, both redesign and moving to a new base. I keep or redirect the page addresses so the site does not lose its Google rankings, and move the tracking without a gap.

faq.q: Who owns the site after handover?
faq.a: You do. Domain, hosting, Google accounts and the admin are registered to you; I only keep working access. Nothing is lost if you ever change supplier.

page.geo: When a site is down, every day costs something. I am in Bratislava, in your time zone and on your working hours, so there is no waiting until morning for someone on the other side of the world to wake up. The invoice carries a Slovak company number, and when something has to be sorted with a Slovak host or registrar, I speak their language.

faq.q: How much does a fix cost?
faq.a: The hourly rate is 35 EUR. Most ordinary faults take one to three hours. I estimate after diagnosis, before starting.

faq.q: How fast can you fix it?
faq.a: Most faults the same day. For anything more involved I give a date right after diagnosis.

faq.q: Will you fix a site you did not build?
faq.a: Mostly those. WordPress, Shoptet, PHP, Python, JavaScript, the platform does not matter.

faq.q: Do you need access?
faq.a: Yes, to the admin and ideally the hosting over FTP or SSH. If you have lost the access, I can help recover it.

faq.q: What if the site is hacked?
faq.a: Back up the current state, remove the malicious code, close the hole it came through, then set up protection. Cleaning without closing the hole is pointless.

faq.q: Is there a guarantee?
faq.a: Yes. If the same fault returns, I deal with it without another invoice.

page.lead: Google Ads and Meta can bring enquiries on day one, unlike SEO where results take months. There is one condition: it has to be visible what comes back. Without tracking wired up properly the budget goes out blind and automated bidding has nothing to learn from.
process: Measurement first, campaigns second. Running ads without conversion tracking means paying for data nobody collects.
A look at competitors: what they bid on, what they promise and roughly what it costs.
A budget calculated from click prices and real conversion rates rather than guessed.
Accounts, campaigns and creatives, including Merchant Center for shops.
Links to GA4, Search Console and the site, so conversions feed back into the system.
Optimisation once data accumulates, then scaling what works.
cases: A campaign running without conversion tracking: Google has nothing to optimise towards and spends on the cheapest clicks.
Broad match with no negatives: paying for queries unrelated to the business.
Ads pointing at the home page instead of the page about that specific service.
One budget covering brand and non-brand queries: brand eats most of it and it looks like success.
No Consent Mode, so a share of conversions is never counted and the campaign looks unprofitable.
page.geo_title: The Slovak market has its own prices
page.geo: Click prices, competition and buyer behaviour in Slovakia differ from larger markets. A budget copied from a foreign guide does not work here. I have worked here for over ten years and know what a click costs in your field and whether ads make sense at all. If they do not, I say so before you spend.

faq.q: What does campaign setup cost?
faq.a: The hourly rate is 25 EUR and a full launch starts around 1,000 EUR. Ad spend is separate and paid directly to Google or Meta.

faq.q: What budget do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the field and click prices. I calculate it from real figures for your market and name the minimum below which launching is pointless.

faq.q: When will I see results?
faq.a: First enquiries can arrive on launch day, but a meaningful read needs two to four weeks of data.

faq.q: Why insist on tracking before launch?
faq.a: Because without it nobody knows which clicks brought money, and automated bidding has nothing to learn from. It is the most expensive saving in online marketing.

faq.q: Do you manage campaigns ongoing?
faq.a: Yes. After launch continuous optimisation matters, without it a campaign loses performance over time.

faq.q: How much does Google advertising cost per month?
faq.a: A budget for one service in one city is €10 to 15 a day, so €300 to 450 a month, plus management by the hour. Less also works, but the statistics take three times longer to collect and you pay all that time without data to decide on.

faq.q: Google Ads or Facebook: where to start?
faq.a: Google where people already search for the service: repairs, servicing, legal and accounting, local services. Meta where demand has to be created: a new product, food, beauty, events. With one budget I start with search, because a lead from it is cheaper to verify.

faq.q: Do you run ads for online stores?
faq.a: Yes: Merchant Center, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns linked to the store catalogue and purchase tracking in GA4, so the budget moves towards the products that actually sell.

facts.label: statistics and access stay with you

page.lead: Most companies run analytics that counts visits but cannot say how many enquiries the site produced. That is not a detail: without proper measurement decisions are guesswork and ad spend is optimised blind. I set up GA4, Tag Manager and conversion tracking so the numbers match reality.
process: An audit of what you have. Very often events turn out to go nowhere, or to be counted twice.
Google Tag Manager and GA4 with Consent Mode v2, so measurement survives the cookie banner.
The events that matter: form submissions, phone, email and WhatsApp clicks, checkout starts.
Marking key events, so enquiries appear as conversions rather than sitting in a list.
Links to Google Ads and Search Console, so it is visible what brings money.
Microsoft Clarity for recordings and heatmaps, where numbers are not enough.
cases: Events pushed to the dataLayer with no GA4 tag in the container to forward them, so enquiries are not measured at all.
GA4 loaded twice, once directly and once through Tag Manager, doubling every page view.
A form firing a 'purchase' event with a value when nobody paid, putting revenue that never existed into the reports.
A key event left unmarked, so conversions read zero while enquiries keep arriving.
A cookie banner blocking measurement where it need not, quietly losing data.
page.geo: Analytics in Slovakia is not purely technical. Without consent wired up per Consent Mode v2 you lose data and Google restricts remarketing, and the consent itself has to take the form European rules require. I set up both at once, so neither is sacrificed for the other.

faq.q: What does an analytics setup cost?
faq.a: The hourly rate is 25 EUR, and a full setup for an ordinary company site starts around 500 EUR. I quote after a short audit of what you already have.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Two to five working days for an ordinary site including testing. Longer for a shop with purchase tracking.

faq.q: How will I know measurement actually works?
faq.a: I show you the events arriving in the real-time report and we go through what each one means.

faq.q: Do I need server-side tracking?
faq.a: Not everyone does. It pays off for larger shops and where ad blockers eat a meaningful share of the data. I will tell you honestly whether it is worth it for you.

faq.q: Will I lose historical data?
faq.a: No. The setup does not change what has already been collected, only what is collected from now on.

cookies.seo_desc: A custom cookie banner under EU rules with Consent Mode v2 from 200 € one-off, no monthly plugin subscription. Measurement stays accurate after a refusal.
cookies.seo_keywords: cookie banner, consent mode v2, gdpr slovakia, cookie setup, google consent mode

page.lead: If your site runs analytics or advertising, cookie consent is mandatory, and not just any consent. Since March 2024 Google requires Consent Mode v2; without it you lose data and remarketing is restricted. I build a custom banner that meets the rules and carries no monthly subscription.
process: A banner in your site's own style, not a third-party module bolted on top.
Consent Mode v2 wired correctly into Google Analytics, Tag Manager and the ad accounts.
Consent split into analytics, advertising and functional, not one 'accept everything' button.
The visitor's choice stored, and changeable at any time.
Testing across more than fifteen scenarios: accept, reject, partial consent, repeat visit.
A cookie policy page written to match.
cases: Ready-made tools charge a monthly subscription forever; a custom banner is a one-off.
Most plugins block measurement more than they need to, losing data even where consent was given.
A third-party module slows the site down, which Google reflects in rankings.
With a ready-made tool you do not control what fires when, and that is exactly what decides whether Consent Mode works.
The design cannot be matched to the site without paying extra.
page.geo: The duty to ask for consent does not come from Slovak law but from European rules: GDPR and the ePrivacy directive. Slovakia adopts them, but they are read the same way across the Union. In practice consent must be freely given, specific and revocable, and measurement may only start afterwards. I set it up so you meet the rules and do not lose data needlessly.

faq.q: What does a cookie banner cost?
faq.a: From 200 EUR, one-off. No monthly subscription.

faq.q: Do I need one if I only run Google Analytics?
faq.a: Yes. Analytics cookies require consent too. Only strictly necessary technical cookies are exempt.

faq.q: What happens without one?
faq.a: You risk a fine from the supervisory authority, and Google restricts remarketing while a share of conversions goes uncounted.

faq.q: Will it ruin my statistics?
faq.a: Some data is naturally lost on refusal, but Consent Mode v2 allows modelling to fill the gap. A badly configured banner loses far more.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually two to three working days including testing.

facts.label: a lawful banner, installed on your site
consent wired into Google and your measurement

audit.seo_title: Free SEO audit: manual website check within 3 days
audit.seo_desc: A free SEO audit by a person, not a scanner: indexing, speed, queries, enquiry tracking. A written list of findings ranked by impact within 3 working days, no obligation.
audit.h1: Free SEO audit of your website
audit.lead: I go through your site the way Google sees it and tell you exactly what stops it bringing you customers. No fee, no obligation.
audit.what_title: What a website SEO audit is
audit.what_text: A technical check of the site through a search engine’s eyes: whether Google sees all of it, how fast it loads, which queries it appears for and what is holding it back. Some call it a technical website audit, others a website evaluation or an SEO check — it is the same thing. The audit itself repairs nothing: it names what is wrong, what fixing it costs and in what order to do it.
audit.why_text: Because it is the most honest way to start. Most sites carry two or three technical faults that quietly take most of the traffic, and until you see them there is no point discussing the price of anything else. Fix them yourself and I am glad. Don't, and at least you know exactly what you are buying.
check_points: Technical foundation: status codes, redirects, www and non-www versions, HTTP against HTTPS — the faults that can make a site invisible to Google.
Indexing: how many pages are actually in Google, which are missing and why. Sitemap, robots.txt, canonical, hreflang.
Speed and Core Web Vitals on mobile and desktop, with the actual causes rather than just a score.
Content and queries: what the site shows up for today, at which positions, and what it needs to reach the first page.
Structured data and how the site looks in search results.
Measurement: whether Google Analytics and Tag Manager actually record enquiries or only page views. This is the most common surprise.
Competitors: who holds your queries in Slovakia and what they have that you don't.
get_points: Findings ordered by impact rather than alphabetically — from what costs you most down to the details.
For each finding, what to do about it and how much work it really is.
What you can fix yourself and what needs a change in the code.
An estimate of which fixes pay off soonest.
time_points: Send your website address through the form below.
Within 3 working days you get the audit in writing.
If you want, we go through it together — in person in Bratislava or online.
audit.who_text: Companies in Slovakia whose site exists but brings no enquiries. Online shops paying for ads without knowing what comes back. And anyone whose site was built by someone else and who is not sure it was done properly.
audit.diy_title: Want to look at the site yourself first?
audit.diy_text: The first checks take an hour and require writing to nobody — indexing, duplicate addresses, speed on mobile, and whether enquiries are counted at all. The step-by-step is here:
audit.trust_text: Ing. Kirill Mosin, White Eagles & Co. s.r.o. I have lived in Slovakia for more than 10 years, launched 12+ sites for Slovak companies, and know how buyers and institutions behave here. I invoice with a Slovak company number. We speak Slovak, Russian and English.
audit.cta_title: Want to know what is holding your site back?
audit.cta_text: Send your address — I will come back with the audit within 3 working days.

faq.q: Is the audit really free?
faq.a: Yes. I charge nothing for it and it is not tied to an order. It is a way to meet over real work rather than a presentation.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Up to 3 working days from when you send the address. For large online shops it can take up to 5 days, and I say so in advance.

faq.q: Do you need access to my site?
faq.a: Not for a basic audit: a public address is enough. Access to Google Search Console and Analytics makes it considerably more accurate, because I can see real queries and visitor behaviour.

faq.q: What if I want to fix things myself?
faq.a: Go ahead. The audit is written so it can be worked through without me. If you get stuck, get in touch.

faq.q: Do you audit sites you did not build?
faq.a: Mostly those, in fact. It does not matter whether it runs on WordPress, Shoptet or custom code.

faq.q: What if the site is fine?
faq.a: Then I say so. It is rare, but it happens. In that case the conversation is about content and winning more enquiries, not about repairs.

faq.q: What is the difference between an SEO audit and a technical website audit?
faq.a: In practice the terms overlap. "Technical audit" usually means the narrower scope: code, speed, indexing. I do both at once, because separately there is no way to tell why a site brings no enquiries: a fast site on the wrong queries fails just as surely as a slow one.

faq.q: Does the audit include a consultation?
faq.a: Yes, if you want one. You get the audit in writing and we can then go through it together, in person in Bratislava or online. I charge nothing for a consultation about the audit.

items.q: How much does a website cost in Slovakia?
items.a: A simple landing page with contacts and a form from 1 500€. A full multi-page website with booking or time slots, email on your own domain and enquiry tracking from 3 500€. An e-shop from 5 000€. The development rate is 35€/hr. The final sum depends on the number of pages and languages, integrations (CRM, payments, booking) and the extent of custom design. The price is agreed in advance and does not change mid-project; no complex brief is needed, a short conversation about goals is enough. Included: analytics with enquiry tracking, a cookie banner with Consent Mode v2, the mandatory Slovak company details and 6 months of support.

Verifiable facts: a Slovak s.r.o. with IČO 57098581, issuing a faktúra you can expense; 12+ launched websites for Slovak businesses with live addresses (Biliardovňa, Krása štúdio OK, Top Sklad, Synchro Žralok, BODA BODA); average delivery of 10 working days with 90% of projects done within 15; 6 months of support included; the domain and hosting are registered to the client, not the contractor. One person runs the project from brief to launch. The team works in Slovak, English and Russian.

Six services: web development (landing pages, company sites and e-shops on React/Next.js, PHP and Python), bug fixing and support for existing sites, Google Ads and Meta campaign setup (from 1,000 EUR, 25 EUR/hr), GA4 + Tag Manager analytics with enquiry tracking (from 500 EUR), Telegram bots in Python (from 500 EUR), and Consent Mode v2 cookie banners with no monthly subscription (from 200 EUR).

A landing page takes one to two weeks, a company site two to four, an online shop longer depending on the catalogue and integrations. Average delivery is 10 working days; 90% of projects ship within 15, because no lengthy specification is required - the solution is proposed after a short conversation about the business goals.

items.q: What languages do you work in and how do I pay?
items.a: The team works in Slovak, English and Russian. Payment is by Slovak invoice (faktúra) with IČO and DIČ - deductible as a business expense - by bank transfer, card or cryptocurrency (USDT, Bitcoin). The price is agreed before work starts.

items.q: Do you set up Google Ads for businesses in Slovakia?
items.a: Yes, it is a core service. A full campaign launch starts at roughly 1,000 EUR at a rate of 25 EUR/hr; the advertising budget itself is separate and paid directly to Google or Meta from your own account. The account is registered to you, so the statistics stay yours. Setup covers campaign structure, negative keywords, ads, GA4 conversion tracking and Consent Mode v2, without which Google has not counted part of EU conversions since March 2024.
